﴿And Allah is ever Knowing of all things﴾ Among the totality of which are these rulings and the wisdoms that He has explained to you, and from which you were in doubting suspicion.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 33, verse 41:

﴿O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance﴾ by that which He deserves of tahlil (declaring His oneness, saying "there is no god but Allah"), tahmid (praising Him, saying "all praise is for Allah"), tamjid (glorifying Him), and taqdis (sanctifying Him).

﴿Much remembrance﴾ that encompasses all times and all states.

**﴿And glorify Him﴾**: and declare Him far exalted above whatever is unfitting for Him.

**﴿morning and evening﴾**: that is, at the beginning of the day and at its end. This specification of the two times is not meant to restrict glorification to them alone, to the exclusion of all other times, but rather to show their excellence over all other times, because they are times of witnessing (mashhudayn), like the singling out of tasbih among the remembrances (adhkar) even though it is included among them, since it is the foremost of them (al-'umdah fihā).

It has also been said that both verbs are directed at these two times, as in your saying: "Fast and pray on Friday." And it has been said that what is meant by tasbih is prayer (al-salah).

(p-107) ﴿He it is Who sends blessings upon you﴾ ... etc. This is a resumptive clause (isti'naf) functioning as a causal explanation of the two matters mentioned before it: God's sending blessings upon them despite their not deserving them, and His being free of need from all the worlds. These things necessitate that they persist in what God deserves from them, namely the remembrance and glorification of Him.

As for His saying, ﴿and His angels﴾, it is a conjunction (ʿatf) upon the pronoun hidden in yuṣallī (the verb "sends blessings"), the separation being sufficient to dispense with emphasizing it with a separate pronoun. However, it is not that by ṣalāh is meant mercy first and seeking forgiveness second, for using a single word in two different meanings is not permissible. Rather, it is that by both is meant a general figurative meaning, of which both senses are a true instance: namely, caring for that in which their good lies and the rectification of their affairs. For each of mercy and seeking forgiveness is a true instance of it. Or (it means) compassion and inner inclination (al-infiʿāl al-maʿnawī), derived from ṣalāh, which includes outward inclination (al-infiʿāl al-ṣūrī), which is bowing and prostration. There is no doubt that the angels' seeking forgiveness for the believers and their supplication for them is a form of compassion upon them. As for the claim that this is a cause of mercy because they are answered in supplication, as has been said, its consideration tends toward combining the two different meanings, so reflect.

﴿That He may bring you out of darkness into light﴾: it is connected to "yuṣallī," i.e., He and His angels care for your affairs, so that He may bring you thereby out of the darknesses of disobedience into the light of obedience. His saying, ﴿And He has ever been merciful to the believers﴾, is a parenthetical clause (iʿtirāḍ) confirming the content of what precedes it, i.e., He has been merciful to all the believers, of whom you are part; and for this reason He does with you what He does of caring for your rectification directly and indirectly, and guiding you to faith and obedience. Or: He has been merciful to you, with the description "the believers" placed in the position of the pronoun, in praise of them and to indicate the reason for the mercy. His saying, ﴿

The Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim), on Surah 33, verse 44:

﴿Their greeting on the day they meet Him will be "Peace."﴾ This is an explanation of the deferred rulings (al-ahkam al-ajila) of God's mercy toward them, after an explanation of its immediate effects, which are His care for their affairs and His guidance to obedience, that is, that by which they live. The phrase "their greeting" (تحيتهم) is a verbal noun (masdar, a noun derived from the verb) whose object is attached to it. The day of their meeting Him is at death, or at the resurrection from the graves, or at entry into Paradise. The greeting is a salutation from God, Mighty and Majestic, honoring them, or from the angels as good tidings of Paradise, or as an honor to them. This is like His saying, ﴿And the angels will enter upon them from every gate﴾ ﴿"Peace be upon you"﴾. Or it is an announcement of safety from every disliked thing and calamity. His saying, ﴿and He has prepared for them a generous reward﴾, is an explanation of the effects of His mercy that overflows upon them after their entry into Paradise, following the explanation of the effects of His mercy that reached them before that. Perhaps the choice of the verbal sentence (al-jumla al-fi'liyya) over the nominal sentence (al-jumla al-ismiyya) that corresponds to what precedes it, by saying for example, "and their reward is a generous reward," or "and for them is a generous reward," is for the sake of emphasis in encouraging and kindling desire for what is promised, by showing that the reward, which is the ultimate aim among all the other effects of mercy, is already present, prepared for them, together with what it contains of observance of the verse endings (al-fawasil, the rhyming ends of verses).

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 33, verse 45:

﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness﴾ over those to whom you were sent, observing their conditions, witnessing their deeds, and bearing testimony concerning what proceeds from them of assent and denial and all the other matters of guidance and error in which they are, and discharging that testimony on the Day of Resurrection in a manner that is accepted (p-108) concerning what is for them and what is against them. And it is a *hal muqaddara* (a circumstantial clause describing a state that will come about later).

﴿And a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾ You give good tidings to the believers of Paradise, and you warn the disbelievers of the Fire.

and as one calling to God by His permission, and as a lamp giving light.

Translation of the passage:

﴿And as one calling to Allah﴾ i.e., to the acknowledgment of Him, His oneness, and all the other things whose belief is obligatory concerning His attributes and actions.

﴿by His permission﴾ i.e., by His facilitation. It is figuratively applied to Him, since it is one of its causes. He restricted the calling by it to signal that it is a matter difficult to attain, and a affair extremely hard to accomplish, which cannot be achieved except with support from the Sacred Presence [of God]. How could it not be, when it is turning faces away from the worshipped idols and putting necks into a collar that is unfamiliar?

﴿and as a lamp giving light﴾ by which one is illuminated in the darkness of ignorance and error, and by whose lights one is guided to the paths of right guidance and direction.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 33, verse 47:

﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾ is conjoined (ʿatf) to an implied clause (muqaddar) that the context requires and that the arrangement of the discourse calls for, as if it were said: "So observe the conditions of the people, and give good tidings to the believers among them ﴿that they will have from Allah a great bounty﴾." That is: [great] in rank and nobility over the believers of all other nations, or, in addition to the rewards of their deeds, by way of grace (tafaddul) and beneficence (ihsan).

**﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾** is a prohibition against showing them accommodation (*mudara*, diplomatic leniency) in the matter of the call (*da'wa*, invitation to Islam), against adopting a gentle manner in conveying the message (*tabligh*), and against being lax in warning (*inzar*). He expressed this through the prohibition of obeying them, as an exaggeration in deterrence and in repelling from what is forbidden, by placing it in the same string as them and depicting it in their form. Whoever takes the prohibition as a stirring up and kindling of zeal (*tahyij* and *ilhab*) has strayed far from the true meaning, by many stages.

**﴿And disregard their harm﴾** means: do not care about their harming you because of your firmness in the call and the warning.

**﴿And put your trust in God﴾** in everything you do and everything you leave undone of the affairs, of which this matter is one; for He, exalted is He, is sufficient for you against them.

**﴿And God is sufficient as a Trustee﴾**, the one to whom affairs are entrusted in all circumstances. The mention of the glorious Name in the place of the pronoun serves to give the reason for the ruling and to emphasize the independence of this concluding appositional statement (*i'tiraḍ al-tadhyil*). When the Prophet (ﷺ) was described with five attributes, each was matched with an address appropriate to it, except that he did not explicitly mention the counterpart of "witness," namely the command to watch over (the people), relying on the clarity of the indication of it by the counterpart of "bringer of good tidings," which is the command to give good tidings, as mentioned just before. The "warner" is matched with the prohibition against accommodating the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and against being lax in warning them, as you have realized. The "one who calls to God by His leave" is matched with the command to rely upon Him, insofar as reliance is an expression of seeking support from Him, exalted is He, and seeking help from Him. The "illuminating lamp" is matched with being content with God alone, for whoever God, exalted is He, has strengthened with holy power (*al-quwwa al-qudsiyya*), appointed for prophethood, and made a radiant proof leading people out of the darkness of error into the light of right guidance, is truly worthy of being content with Him alone over everything else.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 33, verse 49:

﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them﴾ That is: before you have had intercourse with them (tumasshuhunna). It is also read tumāssūhunna with a damma on the ta'.

﴿then you have no waiting period for them to count⁠﴾ in days during which they wait on their own account.

﴿that you should compute⁠﴾ you should complete its number, from "I counted the dirhams (ʿaddadtu al-darāhim) and so computed them (iʿtaddahā)." Its real sense is counting it for oneself, just as "I measured it (kiltuhu) and so measured it out for myself (iktālahu)." The attribution to the men is to indicate that the waiting period is the right of the husbands, as the words of the Exalted, ﴿then you have no⁠﴾, suggest. It is also read taʿtaddunahā, with one of the two dals changed to a ta', or it is from iʿtidāʾ (transgression), meaning taʿtadūna fīhā (you transgress regarding it). Seclusion that is valid (al-khalwa al-ṣaḥīḥa) is treated as equivalent to touching.

The specification of believing women, despite the ruling's generality covering the women of the People of the Book, serves to alert that a believer should choose carefully for his seed and should marry only a believing woman. The function of "thumma" (then) is to remove what might be suspected: that the delay of divorce for as long as intercourse would be possible affects the waiting period just as it affects lineage.

﴿So provide for them⁠﴾ that is: if no dowry was specified for her in the contract; for the one for whom a dowry was specified, what is obligatory is half of the specified dowry, not the provision (al-mutʿa), since the provision is recommended according to one narration in our school, and according to another it is not recommended.

﴿and release them⁠﴾ send them out of your houses, since you have no waiting period over them.

﴿a fair release⁠﴾ without harm, and without withholding any right. It is not permissible to interpret it as the sunni divorce (al-ṭalāq al-sunnī), because that is only possible with women who have been consummated.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 33, verse 50:

﴿O Prophet! Indeed We have made lawful to you your wives whom you have given their due compensation﴾ i.e., their dowries (muhur). For these are the "wages" (ujur) of the marriage bonds (al-abda'). Giving them (itaʼuha) is either handing them over promptly, or naming them in the contract. Whichever it is, restricting the lawfulness of marriage for him (ﷺ) by this is not because the permissibility depends on it, since it is necessarily valid for the contract to be concluded without naming a dowry, in which case the mahr al-mithl (the customary dowry) or a provision (mut'a) becomes obligatory, whether or not consummation takes place. Rather, it is for preferring what is more excellent and more proper for him (ﷺ), like the restriction of the lawfulness of a slave-woman by her being one taken as captive, in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿and what your right hand possesses of what Allah has bestowed upon you as spoils﴾, for the beginning of the affair of a purchased woman is not established, nor what has happened to her. And like the restriction of paternal cousins by their having emigrated with him, in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts, and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts, who emigrated with you﴾. It is possible that the restriction of permissibility by this applies to him (ﷺ) specifically, and this is supported by the words of Umm Hani bint Abi Talib: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed to me, and I excused myself to him, and he accepted my excuse. Then Allah revealed this verse, so I was not lawful to him, because I had not emigrated with him; I was among the freed (al-Tulaqa')."

﴿and a believing woman﴾ in the accusative, as a conjunction with the object of "We have made lawful" (ahlalna), since its meaning is not the creation of an immediate permission but the announcement of the general permission encompassing what preceded and what follows. It was also read in the nominative, as a subject whose predicate is omitted, i.e., "We have made her lawful to you as well."

﴿if she gives herself to the Prophet﴾ i.e., she makes her womanhood (bud') his possession by whatever expression, without a dowry, if that happens to occur, as its indefiniteness indicates. But not absolutely; rather, when the Prophet (ﷺ) wishes to take her in marriage, as the words of the Mighty and Majestic express: ﴿if the Prophet wishes to marry her﴾, i.e., wishes to take possession of her womanhood in that manner, namely without a dowry, for that from him (ﷺ) takes the place of acceptance. Since this is not an explicit text that her possession by the word "gift" (hibah) constitutes the contract, it was not suitable to be the basis for the dispute over whether a marriage contract is concluded by the word "gift," either affirmatively or negatively. There is disagreement about whether this contract actually occurred. From Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, none of the wives had been obtained by gift. It was said: those given as gifts were four: Maymunah bint al-Harith, Zaynab bint Khuzaymah al-Ansariyyah, Umm Sharik bint Jabir, and Khawlah bint Hakim. His mention (ﷺ) in both places by the title of prophethood, by way of iltifat, is for honour, and to indicate that it is the basis for the establishment of the ruling, so it is specific to him (ﷺ) according to her specificity to him, as the words of His Exalted saying express: ﴿exclusively for you﴾, i.e., the permission for her became exclusively yours, that is, exclusivity. For the active participle in verbal nouns is not rare, like "al-'afiyah" and "al-kadhibah." Or: the permission to take what We have made lawful to you from the mentioned women, under the mentioned conditions, became exclusively yours. The meaning of His Exalted words ﴿apart from the believers﴾, according to the first reading: the ordinary permission in the known manner is not realised for them; rather, what is realised there is permission with the mahr al-mithl. According to the second: the permission of all under the mentioned conditions is not realised for them; rather, what is realised for them is the permission of some of the counted ones in the known manner. It was read "khalisatun" in the nominative, as the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e., "that is exclusivity for you and specialness," or "it" (that woman), or "the gift is exclusive to you," not exceeding the believers, since they are not lawful to them without a dowry, and the gift is not valid; rather the mahr al-mithl becomes obligatory. And His Exalted words ﴿We have indeed known what We have imposed upon them﴾ i.e., upon the believers.

﴿concerning their wives﴾ i.e., with regard to their rights. This is a parenthetical clause confirming what precedes concerning the exclusivity of the mentioned permission to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and its not extending to the believers, by clarifying that there has been imposed upon them of the conditions and rights of the contract what has not been imposed upon him (ﷺ), as honour for him and expansion upon him; i.e., We have known what ought to be imposed upon them regarding the rights of their wives.

﴿and what their right hands possess﴾ and to what limit and what description it is fitting to impose upon them; so We imposed what We imposed in that manner, and We specified you with some of the particularities.

﴿so that there may be no constraint upon you﴾ i.e., no narrowness. The "lam" is connected to "exclusively" with regard to what it contains of the meaning of the permission being established and realised for him (ﷺ), not with regard to its being specific to him (ﷺ), because the basis of the removal of constraint is the first, not the second, which is an expression for the non-establishment of it for others.

﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving﴾ of what is difficult to guard against.

﴿Merciful﴾ and for this reason He has widened the matter in the places of constraint.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 33, verse 51:

﴿You may postpone whom you will of them﴾, i.e., you may delay them and refrain from lying with them.

﴿And you may take to yourself whom you will﴾, and you may draw to yourself whom you will of them and lie with her, or you may divorce whom you will of them and keep whom you will. It has been read as (turji'u) with a hamza, and the meaning is one.

﴿And whomever you seek﴾, i.e., you desire.

﴿of those whom you have set aside﴾, divorced by a revocable divorce.

﴿there is no blame upon you﴾ concerning anything of what has been mentioned. This is a comprehensive division covering the whole purpose, for he either divorces or keeps. If he keeps, he either lies with her or leaves her and divides or does not divide. If he divorces, then either he leaves the set-aside one or he seeks her. It is narrated that he postponed from among them: Sawdah, Juwayriyah, Safiyyah, Maymunah and Umm Habibah. He would divide for them as he willed and in the manner he willed. Among those he took to himself were: 'A'ishah, Hafsah, Umm Salamah and Zaynab. He postponed five and took four to himself. It is narrated that he used to treat them equally, along with what was permitted and granted to him by choice, except Sawdah, for she gave her night to 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with them all, and said: "Do not divorce me, so that I may be raised in the company of your wives."

﴿That﴾, i.e., what has been mentioned of leaving the matter to your will.

﴿is closer to their eyes being comforted, and that they will not grieve, and that they will be pleased with what you have given them, all of them﴾, i.e., closer to the comfort of their eyes and their contentment together, for it is a ruling in which all of them share equally. Then, if you treat them equally, they find it to be a favor from you, and if you prefer some of them, they know that it is by the ruling of Allah, so their souls are reassured by it. It has been read as (tuqirru) with a damma on the ta' and a fatha on (a'yunahunna), and as (tuqarru) in the passive voice. And (kulluhunna) is an emphasis for the nun of (yardayna). It has also been read in the accusative as an emphasis for them.

﴿And Allah knows what is in your hearts﴾, of inner thoughts and impulses, so strive to do good in them.

﴿And Allah is ever Knowing﴾, exceedingly so in knowledge, so He knows everything you reveal and conceal.

﴿Forbearing﴾, He does not hasten with punishment, so do not be deceived by its delay, for it is a respite, not a neglect.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 33, verse 52:

﴿Women are not lawful to you﴾ with the verb written with a ya' (yahillu, "يَحِلُّ"), because the feminine plural is not a true feminine (ta'nith haqiqi) and because a separation intervenes. It is also read with a ta' (tahillu, "تَحِلُّ").

﴿after this﴾ i.e., after the nine. For him, this is like the four for us. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: after these nine whom you gave the choice, and they chose you. It was also said: after their choosing Allah and His Messenger and their contentment with what you give them of closeness and separation.

﴿nor that you exchange them﴾ i.e., that you replace them by deleting one of the two ta's (tatabaddala, "تَتَبَدَّلَ").

﴿for them﴾ i.e., for these nine.

﴿with other wives﴾ by divorcing one of them and marrying another in her place. The word "min" (in "min azwaj," "مِن أزْواجٍ") is extra (mazidah), serving to emphasize the comprehensiveness (istighraq). Allah, exalted is He, willed for them honour and a reward for what they chose and were content with, so He restricted His Messenger to them. They are the nine whom he (ﷺ) left at his death: 'A'ishah bint Abi Bakr, Hafsah bint 'Umar, Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, Sawdah bint Zam'ah, Umm Salamah bint Abi Umayyah, Safiyyah bint Huyayy al-Khaybariyyah, Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah, Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah, and Juwayriyyah bint al-Harith al-Mustaliqiyyah. 'Ikrimah said: the meaning is: women are not lawful to you after the four categories that We made lawful to you by the attributes previously mentioned, namely the Bedouin women and the strangers, or the People of the Book, or the female slaves through marriage. This is refuted by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿nor that you exchange them﴾, for the meaning of making the mentioned categories lawful is making their marriage lawful, so the meaning of exchanging them must be making the marriage of others lawful in place of making their marriage lawful, and that is only conceivable through abrogation (naskh), which is not among human capacities.

﴿Even if their beauty pleases you﴾ i.e., the beauty of the substituted wives. This is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the subject of "tabaddala" and not from its object, and "min azwaj" is [in the accusative as a specifier] because of its extreme indefiniteness. It was said: its estimation is "their being pleasing to you is supposed," and its verification has already passed in His saying: ﴿and a believing slave-woman is better than a polytheist, even if she pleases you﴾. It was also said: she is Asma' bint 'Umays al-Khath'amiyyah, wife of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, meaning she is among those whose beauty pleased him (ﷺ). It is disputed whether the verse is muhkam (unabrogated) or mansukh (abrogated). It was said: it is abrogated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You may defer whom you will of them and take to you whom you will﴾. It was said: by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed We have made lawful for you﴾. The order of revelation is not according to the order of the mushaf. It was also said: it is abrogated by the Sunnah. "From 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not die until women were made lawful to him." "Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: He (ﷺ) died while [this] was still forbidden."

﴿except what your right hand possesses﴾ is an exception from "women," since it encompasses both wives and slave-women. It was also said that it is a disjunctive exception (munqati').

﴿And Allah is ever, over all things, Watchful﴾: Guardian, Overseer. So beware of transgressing His limits and overstepping His lawful into His unlawful.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 33, verse 53:

(p-112) ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet﴾ This begins an explanation of what people must observe regarding the rights of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, following the explanation of the rights concerning them that the Prophet ﷺ himself must observe. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿unless permission is given to you﴾ is an exceptive clause (istithna' mufarragh) from the most general of circumstances (a'amm al-ahwal), meaning: do not enter them in any circumstance except while you are given permission. It has been said that it is from the most general of times (a'amm al-awqat), meaning: do not enter them at any time except the time when permission is given to you. It has been objected to this that the grammarians stated that occupying the position of an adverb of time (al-wuqu' mawqi' al-zarf) is specific to the explicit verbal noun (al-masdar al-sarih) and not to the interpreted one (al-mu'awwal); one does not say "I will come to you that the rooster crows" but rather "I will come to you at the crowing of the rooster." His saying, exalted is He, ﴿for a meal﴾ is connected to "yu'dhana" (is given permission), by including the meaning of invitation (al-du'a'), to indicate that they should not enter upon the food without an invitation, even if permission has been established, as indicated by His saying, exalted is He, ﴿without waiting for its preparation﴾, meaning: without waiting for its time or its being ready (idrakahu). This is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the subject of "do not enter", on the basis that the exception falls upon both the time and the circumstance together, according to those who permit this. Or it is from the pronoun in "lakum" (for you). It has also been read in the genitive (bi'l-jarr) as an attributive adjective (sifa) of "ta'am" (food), in which case it would be an attribute applied to other than the one it belongs to without the pronoun being made explicit, which has no basis (la masagh lahu) according to the Basrans. It has also been read with imala (inclination), since it is the verbal noun of "anā al-ta'am", meaning: it became ripe (adraka).

﴿But when you are invited, then enter﴾ This is a corrective clause (istidrak) from the prohibition on entering without permission, and in it there is clear evidence that what is meant by permission for the meal is the invitation to it.

﴿And when you have eaten, then disperse﴾: scatter (fa-tafarraqu), and do not linger, because this is an address to a people who used to wait for the meal of the Prophet ﷺ, entering and sitting while awaiting its preparation, specifically for them and their likes. Otherwise it would not be permissible for anyone to enter his houses ﷺ with permission for something other than the meal, nor to remain after the meal for an important matter.

﴿Nor those who linger for conversation﴾, meaning: for the conversation of some of you with one another, or for the conversation of the people of the house by listening to it. It is coordinated with "nazirin" (waiting), or it is governed by an implied verb, meaning: and do not enter, or do not remain, "lingering..." etc.

﴿Indeed, that﴾, meaning: that lingering which you used to do before.

﴿was troubling to the Prophet﴾, due to the narrowing of the dwelling upon him and his family, and its compelling him to occupy himself with what does not concern him, and its preventing him from occupying himself with what does concern him.

﴿and he is shy of you﴾, meaning: of expelling you; because of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and Allah is not shy of the truth﴾. For this implies that the thing one is shy of must be a true matter related to them, not to themselves, and that is none other than their expulsion; so it should not be left out of shyness. For this reason He, exalted is He, did not leave it, and commanded you to leave. The expression of it as "not being shy" is for the sake of parallelism (al-musha-kalah). It has also been read "la yastahi" (without the first yā'), with its vowel transferred to the preceding letter.

﴿And when you ask of them﴾: the pronoun refers to the wives of the Prophet, indicated by the mention of his houses ﷺ.

﴿something﴾, meaning: an item to be enjoyed, from household utensils and other things.

﴿then ask them﴾, meaning: the item.

﴿from behind a partition﴾, meaning: a screen. It is related that 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O Messenger of Allah, the righteous and the wicked enter upon you; so would that you commanded the Mothers of the Believers to observe hijab?" Then this was revealed. It has also been said that the Prophet ﷺ was eating with some of his companions, and the hand of a man among them touched the hand of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and the Prophet disliked that, so this was revealed.

﴿That﴾, meaning: what has been mentioned of not entering without permission, not lingering for conversation upon entering, and asking for items from behind a partition.

﴿is purer for your hearts and their hearts﴾, meaning: more purifying from satanic thoughts.

﴿And it is not for you﴾, meaning: it is not right, nor proper for you.

﴿to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾, meaning: to do during his lifetime an act he dislikes and by which he is distressed.

﴿Nor to marry his wives after him, ever﴾, meaning: after his death or separation.

﴿Indeed, that﴾ refers to what has been mentioned: harming him ﷺ and marrying his wives after him. The sense of distance in it is for signifying the distance of his station in evil and corruption.

﴿was in the sight of Allah an enormity﴾, meaning: a grave matter and a monstrous affair whose magnitude cannot be measured. In it is, of the exaltation by Allah of the status of His Messenger ﷺ and the obligation of his sanctity alive and dead, what is not hidden. For this reason He, exalted is He, emphasized the warning when He said:

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 33, verse 54:

﴿If you disclose a thing﴾, of that which has no good in it, such as marrying them (the wives of the Prophet) by your tongues,

﴿or conceal it﴾ in your breasts.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing of all things﴾, so He will recompense you for what proceeds from you of sins, the manifest and the hidden, without fail. And in this generalization, together with the proof of the intended meaning, there is additional intimidation, severity and exaggeration in the threat.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 33, verse 55:

﴿There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers, nor their sons, nor their brothers, nor the sons of their brothers, nor the sons of their sisters﴾ This is a resumptive statement (isti'naf) to explain who is not required to observe the veil (ihtijab) before them. It is reported that when the verse of the veil was revealed, the fathers, the sons and the relatives said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we also speak to them from behind the veil?" So this was revealed. The paternal uncle and the maternal uncle are not mentioned because they are in the position of the parents; for this reason the paternal uncle is called "father" in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac﴾. Or, it is because mention of them is dispensed with by mentioning the sons of brothers and the sons of sisters, for the basis of the non-obligation of the veil between them (the women) and the two groups is the very same as between them and the paternal and maternal uncles, in terms of paternity and maternity, since they are paternal aunts to the sons of brothers and maternal aunts to the sons of sisters. It is also said: it is because she (the Prophet's wife) disliked abandoning the veil before them both, lest they describe her to their sons.

﴿Nor their women﴾ i.e., the women of the believers.

﴿Nor what their right hands possess﴾ of male slaves and female slaves. It is also said: of female slaves only, and this has been discussed in Surat al-Nur.

﴿And fear Allah﴾ in all that you do and all that you leave undone, especially in what you have been commanded and forbidden.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, Witness﴾ nothing hidden from Him is concealed, and circumstances do not vary in His knowledge.

**Abu al-Su'ud's Commentary (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on Surah 33, Verse 56**

﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels﴾. It is also read as *wa-mala'ikatuhu* (with the nominative *mala'ikatuhu*), coordinated with the place (*mahall*) of *inna* and its noun, according to the Kufans, and as a supposition of an omitted predicate (*khabar*), relying on what follows to indicate it, according to the view of the Basrans.

﴿send blessings upon the Prophet﴾. It has been said: the *salah* (blessing) from Allah is mercy, and from the angels it is asking forgiveness (*istighfar*). Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: it means that Allah shows him mercy, and the angels supplicate for him. And also from him: *yusalluna* means *yubarrikuna* (they bless him). Abu al-'Aliyah said: Allah's *salah* upon him is His praise of him in the presence of the angels, and their *salah* is their supplication for him. Therefore, in *yusalluna* the meaning should be intended as a general sense of "recompense" (*yujazi*), in which each of the aforementioned meanings is a true instance of it, i.e., they take care with what contains his good and the welfare of his affair, and they are keen to manifest his nobility and to magnify his station. That from Allah, glorified is He, is by mercy, and from the angels is by supplication and asking forgiveness.

﴿O you who have believed, send blessings upon him﴾. Take care to do this yourselves as well, for you are more entitled to it.

﴿and greet him with peace (*taslim*)﴾, saying: "O Allah, bless Muhammad and grant him peace," or something similar. It has been said: what is meant by *taslim* is submission to his command. The verse is evidence for the obligation of blessing and peace upon him in general, without addressing whether repetition is obligatory or not. It has been said: this is obligatory whenever his name is mentioned, due to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "May he be humbled into the dust, the man in whose presence I am mentioned and he does not send blessings upon me." And his saying (ﷺ): "Whoever in whose presence I am mentioned and does not send blessings upon me, enters the Fire, and Allah distances him." It is also narrated that he (ﷺ) said: "Allah, exalted is He, has appointed two angels over me, so I am not mentioned in the presence of a Muslim who then sends blessings upon me, except that those two angels say: 'May Allah forgive you,' and Allah, exalted is He, and His angels respond to those two angels: 'Amin.' And I am not mentioned in the presence of a Muslim who does not send blessings upon me, except that those two angels say: 'May Allah not forgive you.' And Allah, exalted is He, and His angels respond to those two angels: 'Amin.'"

Some have said: it is obligatory once in every gathering, even if his name is repeated, as has been said regarding the verse of prostration, the response to one who sneezes (*tashmit al-'atis*), and likewise at the beginning and end of every supplication. Others have said: it is obligatory once in a lifetime, and they said likewise regarding the public declaration of the two testimonies (*shahadatayn*). What caution requires, and what knowledge of the elevation of his exalted station (ﷺ) calls for, is that blessings be sent upon him whenever his noble name is mentioned.

As for sending blessings upon him within the prayer (*salah*), by saying: "O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim, indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious," this is not a condition for the validity of the prayer according to us (the Hanafis). It is narrated from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, may Allah have mercy on him, that the Companions used to suffice with what is in the *tashahhud* (the testimony recited in prayer), which is: "Peace be upon you, O Prophet." As for al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, he made it a condition. As for sending blessings upon anyone other than the prophets, peace be upon them, it is permissible as a follow-on (*taba'an*), but disliked when done independently (*istiqlalan*), because in common usage it is a sign (*shi'ar*) of the remembrance of the messengers. For this reason it was disliked to say "Muhammad, Mighty and Majestic," despite his being mighty and majestic.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 33, verse 57:

﴿Indeed, those who harm Allah and His Messenger﴾ The harm (idha') is meant either as doing what They dislike of disbelief and sins, metaphorically, since actual harm is impossible with respect to Him, exalted is He. It has been said that harming Allah, exalted is He, is the saying of the Jews, the Christians and the polytheists: ﴿The hand of Allah is chained up﴾, and ﴿the third of three﴾, and ﴿the Messiah is the son of Allah﴾, and the angels are the daughters of Allah, and the idols are His partners, exalted is Allah far above that by a great exaltation. It has been said: it is the saying of those who deviate concerning His verses. And harming the Messenger (ﷺ) is their saying: "a poet, a sorcerer, a soothsayer, a madman." It has been said: it is the breaking of his front tooth and the wounding of his noble face on the day of Uhud. It has been said: it is their criticism of his marriage to Safiyya. The truth is that it is general in both of these. As for harming him (ﷺ) specifically in the literal sense, and the mention of Allah, mighty and majestic, is for his glorification and to announce the greatness of his rank with Him, exalted is He, and harming him (ﷺ) is harming Him, glorified is He. ﴿Allah has cursed them﴾: He expelled them and removed them far from His mercy.

﴿In this world and the Hereafter﴾: in such a way that they hardly obtain anything of good in either of them.

﴿And He has prepared for them﴾ in addition to that:

﴿a humiliating punishment﴾ which will befall them in the Hereafter specifically.

﴿And those who harm the believing men and the believing women﴾ do to them what they are hurt by, whether by speech or by deed. The restriction in His words, Exalted is He, ﴿without their having earned it﴾, meaning without any offence that would make them deserve harm, comes after the harm was stated without restriction in what precedes it. This signals that harm done to Allah and His Messenger is never anything but unjust. As for the harm done to these people, some of it is of this kind and some of it is of that kind.

﴿then they have borne a slander and a manifest sin﴾, meaning clear and evident. It has been said that it was revealed concerning hypocrites who used to harm ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, and make him hear what was not good. It has also been said that it was revealed concerning the people of the slander (al-ifk). Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Kalbī said that it was revealed concerning adulterers who would follow women when they went out at night to attend to their needs. They would only approach female slaves, but it may sometimes have happened that they also approached free women, out of ignorance or feigned ignorance, because all of them were alike in their outer garments and clothing. The apparent meaning is that the verse is general to all of what has been mentioned, and to what the spreaders of rumours (al-murjifūn) will say later on.

O Prophet, after explaining the bad state of those who cause harm, in order to deter them from harming others, commanded the Prophet (ﷺ) to tell some of those who were harmed by them to adopt what would in general prevent their harm, namely covering themselves and being distinguished from the places where harm occurs. So it was said: ﴿Say to your wives, your daughters, and the women of the believers: let them draw their jalabib (outer garments) over themselves﴾. The jilbab (a garment wider than the khimar, the head-covering) is a cloth that a woman wraps around her head, leaving part of it to fall over her chest. It was also said that it is the milhafa (wrap), and everything with which one covers oneself. That is, they should cover their faces and bodies with it when they go out for any of the reasons that call for going out. The word ﴿min﴾ ("from") here is partitive, because it has been mentioned that the customary practice is to wrap oneself with part of it and let part of it hang down. It is reported from al-Suddi: she covers one of her eyes, her forehead, and the other side, except for the eye.

﴿That﴾ means: what has been mentioned of covering.

﴿is nearer﴾, closer, ﴿to their being recognized﴾ and distinguished from the slave women and the singing girls, who are the places where men encounter and harm them.

﴿So that they will not be harmed﴾ by the people of illicit desire through approaching them.

﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving﴾ of what has passed from them of negligence,

﴿Merciful﴾ toward His servants, since He takes into consideration for their welfare such particulars as these.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 33, verse 60:

﴿If the hypocrites do not desist﴾ from what they are upon of hypocrisy and its rulings that necessitate causing harm.

﴿And those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ from what they are upon of wavering and what follows from it of that which holds no good.

﴿And the agitators in the city﴾ from among the two groups, from what they are upon of spreading bad news about the expeditions of the Muslims and other fabricated rumours that entail harm. The root of irjaf (agitation) is tahrik (stirring), from rajfah, which is tremor (zalzalah); false news is described by it because it is shaking and unstable.

﴿Then We would surely incite you against them﴾ meaning, We would surely command you to fight them and expel them, or to do what compels them to leave, and We would surely urge you to that.

﴿Then they will not remain as your neighbours﴾ is a conjunction upon the answer of the oath, and "then" (thumma) indicates that expulsion and separation from the neighbourhood of the Messenger (ﷺ) is the greatest of what befalls them.

﴿therein﴾ i.e., in the city.

﴿except for a little﴾ a limited time, or a little neighbourhood, until their state becomes clear as to whether they desist or not.

"Mal'unin" (cursed) is in the accusative, either as a term of censure (*shatm*, a form of vituperative accusative) or as a circumstantial state (*hal*), on the basis that the exception (*istithna'*) also applies to it, according to the opinion of those who permit this, as passed in His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿not waiting for its ripeness﴾. There is no way for it to be governed by His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿Wherever they are found, they shall be seized and slain with a thorough slaying﴾, because what follows the conditional particle does not operate on what precedes it. (p-116)

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 33, verse 62:

﴿Such has been the way of Allah with those who passed away before, and you will never find any change in the way of Allah.﴾ That is: Allah established this as a way (sunnah) among the earlier nations, namely that He would kill those who were hypocrites toward the prophets, peace be upon them, and who strove to weaken their cause by spreading rumors and the like, wherever they were found.

﴿And you will never find any change in the way of Allah.﴾ That is, a fundamental principle (asl), because it is founded upon the basis of wisdom (hikmah), around which the orbit of legislation (tashri') revolves.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 33, verse 63:

﴿The people ask you about the Hour.﴾ That is, about the time of its establishment. The polytheists used to ask the Prophet (ﷺ) about this, hastening it by way of mockery, and the Jews asked to test him, because God Most High had concealed its time in the Torah and the rest of the Books.

﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with God.﴾ He does not reveal it to any angel brought near, nor to any prophet sent. And His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And what will make you know?﴾ is a separate address to him (ﷺ), not included under the command, and it is brought to show that, although its time is unknown to creation, its coming is expected soon. That is: what will inform you of the time of its establishment? That is, nothing at all will inform you of it.

﴿Perhaps the Hour is near.﴾ That is: something near, or the Hour will be at a near time. Its accusative is adverbial (ẓarfiyyah, of time), and the masculine form may be used in view of the Hour being understood as "the Day" or "the time." In it there is a warning to those who hasten, a rebuke to those who seek to trap, and the (explicit noun) "the Hour" in place of a pronoun serves to inspire awe, to increase the affirmation, and to emphasize the independence of the sentence, as has been indicated.

Abu al-Su'ud, Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim (Tafsir Abi al-Su'ud), on surah 33, verse 64:

﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers﴾ without restriction, that is, He has expelled them and removed them far from His mercy, both in this world and in the next.

﴿And has prepared for them, in addition to that, a blazing fire﴾, a fire of intense burning, which they will endure in the Hereafter.

Abu al-Su'ud's commentary (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 33, verse 65:

﴿Abiding therein forever; they shall find no protector﴾ who would guard them, ﴿nor any helper﴾ who would deliver them from it.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 33, verse 66:

﴿On the Day their faces are turned over in the Fire﴾ is an adverbial complement (zarf) governing "lack of finding" (la-'adam al-wijdan). It has also been said that it governs "abiding therein" (khalidin), and it has been said that it governs "helper" (nasiran), and it has been said that it is an object of "remember" (udhkur), meaning: on the Day their faces are turned about in it from one side to another, like meat being roasted in the fire, or being cooked in the cooking-pot so that the boiling turns it about from one side to another, or from one state to another; or they will be cast into it face-down and upside-down. It has been read as "tuqallabu" with one of the two taa' removed from "tatqallabu." And it has been read as "nuqallibu," with the verb attributed to the nun of majesty (nun al-'azamah) and "their faces" in the accusative; and as "tuqallibu," with the verb attributed to the Blaze (al-sa'ir). The singling out of the faces for mention is because they are the most honoured of the limbs, so it contains an added intensification of the horror of the matter and an amplification of the gravity of the affair. It is also permissible that it be an expression for the whole body.

Then the words of Him, exalted is He: ﴿They say﴾ is a resumptive clause (isti'naf) built upon a question arising from the depiction of their dreadful state, as if it were said: "What do they do at that time?" So it is said: they say, full of regret over what has escaped them: ﴿Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger!﴾ so that we would not be afflicted with this punishment. Or it is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun of "their faces," or from "it" itself, or it is the governing element of "on the Day."

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 33, verse 67:

﴿And they will say﴾ It is coordinated (ʿatf) with "yaqūlūn" (they say). The shift to the past tense (ṣīghat al-māḍī) indicates that this statement of theirs is not continuous as their earlier statement was, but is rather a kind of excuse, by which they intended a form of gloating (tashaffī) through doubling the punishment of those who led them into that predicament, even though they knew it would not be accepted in regard to their own deliverance from it.

﴿Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters (sādatanā) and our elders (kubarāʾanā)﴾ meaning their leaders who inculcated disbelief in them. It is also read as "sādātinā" (our masters, in the plural), to indicate abundance. Describing them with the title of mastery and greatness serves to strengthen the excuse; otherwise they are in a position of contempt and humiliation.

﴿So they led us astray from the way﴾ by means of the falsehoods they made appealing to us. The "alif" (in al-sabīlā) is for pausal lengthening (al-iṭlāq), as in ﴿wa-aṭaʿnā al-rasūlā﴾ (and we obeyed the Messenger).

"Our Lord, give them double the punishment, (i.e., twice the punishment We gave to them) because they went astray and led others astray.

﴿And curse them with a great curse﴾, i.e., a severe, mighty curse. It is also read as "a multitude of curses" (kathiran). The opening of the supplication with the (repeated) address "Our Lord" is for the sake of intensifying the entreaty and the pleading, and for summoning the response."

**Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on Surah 33, verse 69:**

﴿O you who have believed, do not be like those who abused Moses﴾. It is said: it was revealed concerning Zayd and Zaynab, and what was heard about her from the people's talk. ﴿But Allah cleared him of what they said﴾, meaning: He made manifest his innocence (ﷺ) of what they said about him, that is, of its content. Its import, which is the blameworthy matter, was that Qarun (Korah) incited a prostitute to accuse him (peace be upon him) by herself, by giving her a great amount of money. Allah the Exalted made manifest his (peace be upon him) freedom from that, by the prostitute confessing to the bribe that had taken place between her and Qarun, and what was done to Qarun was done, as explained in Surah al-Qasas.

It is also said: some people accused him of killing Harun when he went out with him to Mount Tur, and Harun died there. The angels carried him and passed by him until they saw him not killed. It is also said: Allah the Exalted brought him back to life, and he informed them of his innocence. It is also said: they accused him of a defect in his body, either leprosy or a swelling of the testicles, due to his extreme concealment out of modesty. So Allah the Exalted made them aware of his innocence, by the stone running off with his garment when he put it down while bathing. The story is well known.

﴿And he was honorable (wajihan) in the sight of Allah﴾, meaning: possessing nearness and standing. It was also read as (وَكانَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ وجِيهًا), "and he was a servant of Allah, honorable."

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 33, verse 70:

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah﴾ i.e., in everything you do and everything you leave undone, especially in committing what He dislikes, let alone what would harm His Messenger (ﷺ).

﴿And speak﴾ in every matter of affairs.

﴿words of appropriate justice﴾ aiming at the truth, from sadda, yasiddu, sidad (to hit the mark), as one says: "saddada al-sahm nahwa al-ramiyyah" (he aimed the arrow toward the target) when he did not turn it away from its direction. The intended meaning is forbidding them from what they had been engaged in of the statement about Zaynab that deviated from justice and rectitude.

Yuṣliḥ lakum aʿmālakum (ﷻ): "He will set right your deeds for you." That is, He will guide you to righteous deeds, or He will make them sound by accepting them and granting reward for them.

Wa-yaghfir lakum dhunūbakum: "And He will forgive you your sins," and will make them expiated by your uprightness in speech and action.

Wa-man yuṭiʿi Allāh wa-rasūlahu: "And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger," in the commands and prohibitions, of which these obligations are a part.

Faqad fāza: "then he has indeed attained success," in both abodes, fawzan ʿaẓīman: "a great success," whose measure cannot be estimated and whose end cannot be reached.

(p-118) ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it.﴾ When he (may Allah be exalted) had explained the great importance of obeying Allah and His Messenger, by stating the fate of those who depart from it, which is a painful punishment, and the attainment of those who observe it, which is a great triumph, he followed this with an explanation of the great importance of what makes it obligatory, namely the legal obligations, and of the difficulty of their matter, by way of a parable. This is accompanied by an indication that what proceeded from them of obedience and of abandoning it proceeded after their acceptance and commitment. He expressed these obligations by the term "trust" to draw attention to the fact that they are rights to be safeguarded, which Allah the Exalted deposited with the responsible persons (mukallafin), entrusted them with, and made it incumbent upon them to receive them with good obedience and submission, and commanded them to observe and guard them and to discharge them without neglecting any of their rights. He expressed their consideration, in relation to the readiness of the aforementioned heavens and the rest, by "offering" them, to demonstrate the utmost care given to their matter and the desire for those beings to accept them; and their unreadiness to accept them, by "refusing" and "being apprehensive" of them, to magnify their matter and to exalt its dignity; and their acceptance of them, by "bearing," to realize the sense of difficulty considered in them, by making them of the kind of heavy bodies upon which bodily powers are employed, the strongest and greatest of which is the strength and might that are in those beings. The meaning is that the trust is of such great importance that, had those great bodies, which are a parable of strength and might, been charged with observing it, and had they been possessed of consciousness and perception, they would have refused to accept it and been apprehensive of it. But the discourse has been turned away from its usual course, by depicting the supposed as if it were realized, in order to increase the realization of the intended meaning through the parable and to clarify it.

﴿And man bore it﴾, i.e., at the time of its being offered to him, either by considering it in relation to his readiness, or by his being charged with it on the Day of the Covenant (yawm al-mithaq); that is, he undertook it and committed himself to it, despite the weakness of his constitution and the feebleness of his strength. This is either an expression of his acceptance of it in accordance with his innate readiness (istidad fitri), or an expression of his acknowledgment by his saying "Yes" (bala). And His statement (exalted is He): ﴿Indeed, he was wrongdoing, ignorant﴾ is a parenthetical clause (i'tirad) inserted between the bearing and its end, to indicate from the very outset that he would not fulfill what he pledged and undertook; that is, he was excessive in wrongdoing and extreme in ignorance, namely according to the majority of his individuals who did not act in accordance with the requirement of their sound nature or their previous acknowledgment, and not those others who did not alter the nature of Allah (fitrat Allah) at all. It is to the first group that reference is made by His statement (exalted is He):

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 33, verse 73:

﴿So that Allah may punish the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and the polytheist women﴾. That is: man bore it so that Allah might punish some of its individuals who did not observe it and did not meet it with obedience. This is on the basis that the *lām* (ل) is of consequence (*lām al-ʿāqibah*, the *lām* denoting outcome). Although punishment was not the purpose of bearing the trust, it followed from it for some of its individuals, and so it was presented in the form of a purpose, as purposes follow from acts that are explained by them. That is: the consequence of man's bearing it was that Allah the Exalted would punish those of his individuals who betrayed the trust and completely left obedience. The second group is indicated by His saying: ﴿and that Allah may turn in mercy to the believing men and the believing women﴾. That is: the consequence of his bearing it was that Allah the Exalted would turn in mercy to those of his individuals, that is, He would accept their repentance, because they did not wholly remove the yoke of obedience from their necks, and because they made up for the lapses that occurred from them, which a human being rarely avoids by virtue of his nature, by repenting and turning back. The shift (*al-iltifāt*) to the Majestic Name at first is to magnify the gravity of the matter and to cultivate awe. The use of an explicit noun in place of a pronoun the second time is to highlight the greater concern for the matter of the believers, in order to give each of the two stations, that of threat and that of promise, its due. And Allah knows best.

He made the trust, whose nature is that it should come from Him the Exalted, a reference to obedience, which is among the acts of the responsible persons that follow from the obligation. This is far from what is near. The statement was taken as confirming the gracious promise indicated by His saying: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly achieved a great achievement﴾. The exaltation of the status of obedience serves as a means to that, on the ground that whoever upholds the rights of such a great matter and observes them is worthy of attaining the good of both abodes. This is rejected by its description of man as wrongdoing and ignorant at first, and by the reasoning for bearing it as the punishment of one group and the turning in mercy toward another group second. It was said: the intended meaning of "trust" is unrestricted submission, encompassing the natural and the voluntary. By "presenting it" is meant its being solicited, which includes demanding the act from the one who chooses it and the will for its occurrence from another. By "their bearing it" is meant betrayal of it and refraining from fulfilling it. Thus refusing (*al-ibāʾ*) is abstention from betrayal and coming with what is intended. The meaning is that these bodies, despite their greatness and strength, refused to betray their trust and came with what they were commanded, as in His saying: ﴿We came willingly﴾; while man betrayed it when he did not come with what We commanded him, "Indeed he was a wrongdoer, ignorant." It was said: when Allah the Exalted created these bodies, He created in them understanding, and said to them: "I have imposed an obligation, and I have created a Paradise for whoever obeys Me in it, and a Fire for whoever disobeys Me." They said: "We are subjected to what You created us for; we cannot bear an obligation, and we seek neither reward nor punishment." When He created Adam, peace be upon him, He presented the same to him, and he bore it. He was a wrongdoer to himself by taking on what burdens it, and ignorant of the severity of its outcome. It was said: the intended meaning of "trust" is reason or the obligation. "Presenting it to them" means considering it in relation to their readiness, and "their refusal" is natural refusal, which is lack of fitness and readiness for it. "Man's bearing it" means his capacity and readiness for it, and his being a wrongdoer and ignorant is because the irascible and appetitive powers dominated him. This is close to the truth, so reflect. And Allah is the Granter of success. It is also read as (وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ) as a resumed sentence (*al-istiʾnāf*, a new independent clause).

﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful﴾: exceedingly so in forgiveness and mercy, in that He turned in mercy to them, forgave their lapses, and rewarded with success for their acts of obedience.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Ahzab and teaches it to his family and to those whom his right hand possesses, will be given security from the punishment of the grave." And Allah knows best.
